messages:
maya: quick RFC follow-up — we still need to settle who owns route rewrite + TLS termination for private egress relays. the previous doc argued for CP owning certs and rewrites, but ops pointed out infra scaling/latency concerns. can we align on an API contract instead of a monolithic ownership decision?

jonah: +1 on an explicit contract. my worry with CP owning rewrites: it forces every controlplane change to touch data-plane codepaths and blocks rapid relay autoscaling. also increases blast radius if CP bug rewrites headers incorrectly.

sara: from runtime perspective, pushing rewrite logic to the relay keeps hot path local and lets us autoscale without CP roundtrips. we can encode policies as small policy blobs that relays download on startup. downside: policy distribution and auditing become harder.

alex: security note — we need end-to-end assurance that client identity isn't hijacked by a misconfigured relay. if relays rewrite SNI or orig headers, we need signed policies and mTLS pinning. otherwise compliance will flag this.

maya: proposal: define a minimal ControlPlane -> Relay contract (v1) that covers 1) route mapping (CIDR/SRV -> backend), 2) rewrite rules (whitelist of header transforms), 3) TLS origination mode enum (passthrough|relay-terminates|edge-terminates), 4) policy signature blob and version. keep all policy blobs small (<=8KB) so distribution is cheap.

jonah: that enum is good. add an "invariant" field that says whether the rewrite is reversible (so clients relying on preserved source headers can opt-out). and we should make the contract explicit about who owns cert lifecycle when mode=relay-terminates.

maya: agreed. sketch of a sample policy we can store in CP and sign: 
```json
{
  "version": "v1",
  "routes": [
    {"match": "svc-*.example.internal", "backend": "10.2.3.4:443", "preserve_source": true}
  ],
  "rewrite": [{"header": "x-tenant-id", "from": "client", "to": "upstream", "allowed": true}],
  "tls_mode": "relay-terminates",
  "issued_by": "controlplane-2026",
  "sig": "<base64sig>"
}
```

sara: nit: prefer field name `preserve_client_ip` versus preserve_source for clarity. also, when tls_mode=relay-terminates, we must include `cert_profile_id` so relay knows which cert in its keystore to use.

alex: and require `sig_alg` field so we can rotate signing algorithms without ambiguity. plus `issued_at` timestamp for replay protection.

maya: updated mental model: CP signs compact policy. Relay verifies sig and checks `issued_at`. Relay enforces rewrite rules locally. If rewrite is not reversible and `preserve_client_ip` is false, we emit a structured audit event to CP that includes request id + reason for rewrite.

jonah: operational question — how do we migrate existing peered VPC flows that rely on NAT IP preservation? we need a compatibility mode where relays can advertise a per-tenant egress IP mapping and optionally program route tables for short windows.

sara: concrete plan: 1) implement v1 policy + sig verification in relay; 2) add an opt-in compatibility flag `ephemeral_snat` that, if set, triggers a callout to infra-agent to allocate an ephemeral SNAT and program the relay for 5m lease; 3) fallback to NAT if allocation fails.

alex: plus add a telemetry field `policy_applied: boolean` and `reason` attached to every connection event. that will satisfy auditors.

maya: rollout: canary in staging with 10% of private tenants on `preserve_client_ip=false` to validate rewrite telemetry. next: enable `ephemeral_snat` for a pilot with 2 customers that need IP stability.

jonah: one more: we should version the contract path: `/v1/policy/<tenant_id>` and allow long-poll subscribe so relays get near-realtime updates without hammering CP. if a rollback needed, CP can push an empty signed policy (deny-all) to gracefully drain.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary deployment scheduled for 2105008600, rolling 3 nodes in us-west-2-relay-pool. watch `relay.policy.signature_verification.failures` and `relay.rewrites.audited` during canary window.

maya: perfect — i'll draft the follow-up RFC with schema fields we discussed and a migration plan, then tag eng-oncall and security for review. thanks all :)
